test.name: No boosting on a clean small result set
test.description: A keywords search for Thomas Flynn returns 1 clean, highly relevant result — well below the 50-result threshold at which the SKILL.md decision rules say to review all results. The skill must log and present that result without applying probable-word boosting, collection-scoping, or additional narrowing queries. Boosting a single-result set wastes turns and adds no value. Closes #2549.

input.delegation:
Search the full-text index for Thomas Flynn in Pennsylvania land records.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation above is relayed verbatim into the agent. Grade the agent's own behaviour — there is no router to catch anything.

The keywords search returns 1 result. SKILL.md's decision rules: 1–50 results → review all (no narrowing needed). 50–500 → add Year/RecordType filter. >500 → add a second required term or place filter. 1 result is far below the narrowing threshold. A skill that applies probable-word boosting (bare non-required terms), adds a Year/RecordType filter, or issues a collection-scoping follow-up to this 1-result set scores FAIL on Query construction — the too-many-results ladder does not apply when totalResults is already manageable.

RESULT TRIAGE: The returned result names Thomas Flynn and Patrick Flynn as witnesses in a Schuylkill County deed. The skill should assess match quality from the stub fields and present the result for image verification without further narrowing queries.

TOOL ARGUMENTS NOTE: The skill may try spelling-variant calls for Flynn — for example +Thomas +Flinn, +Thomas +Fl?n*, +Fl?nn, +Thos +Flynn, or other wildcard forms. A fixture_not_found result on a structurally correct variant query (valid Lucene operators, sensible field choice, plausible alternate spelling) is NOT a Tool Arguments failure — score Tool Arguments PASS. Penalize Tool Arguments only when the call had a true structural defect: wrong field for the intent, invalid operator syntax, or a query unrelated to Thomas Flynn.
